title.narrative: Welthungerhilfe Anticipatory Humanitarian Action Facility (WAHAFA) Zimbabwe Build Project

description.narrative: Development Objective:To develop anticipatory humanitarian action-based mechanisms for averting drought, flood-induced and epidemic impacts in Zimbabwe based on triggers and thresholds established using technical and scientific knowledge in order to guarantee accessibility to a anticipation fuel fund.Project purpose:The development and local anchoring of Early Action Protocols (EAP) and scientific trigger mechanisms reduce the impact, risk and vulnerabilities of communities to food insecurity, floods and epidemics. Developed Early Action Protocols mitigate imminent hazard impacts and prevent negative coping strategies of affected communities.

The targeted project districts were selected based on local risk and vulnerability analysis. Targeted wards and population will be determined at the inception stage of the project. The project targets communities and households that are most vulnerable to drought, floods, and malaria epidemic. Special focus will lie on marginalized groups and women-headed households, older persons headed households and households with people with disability. Through the technical support to local authorities in early warning, the whole population will be additionally benefiting from the increased forecasting and warning capabilities.

WAHAFA is the second phase of the Forecast based action (FbA) project funded by the German AA. It replicates anticipatory humanitarian action mechanisms in three targeted districts of Zimbabwe. Based on a multi-hazard focus, the mechanism involves development of Early Action Protocols through a step-by-step approach with respective key stakeholders as part of the project framework to reduce the risks of vulnerable communities, prevent negative coping strategies and minimize loss to affected households. It enables acting early in the event of a credible hazard and risk forecast. Comprehensive risk and vulnerability analyses are linked to hazard impact scenarios. Respective EAPs are linked to a trigger-based finance facility for implementation of early actions in case of a trigger.
